what_was_actually_missing: The task list marked this item complete on the strength of a working-tree file that had never been committed and was never recorded in task_plan.md. deliverable.conclusion: tests/test_model_extensions_anchor.py is a new, independent, minimal regression that anchors the eight extension models to the product registry. It is now committed.
deliverable.why_this_is_the_right_regression: tests/test_model_extensions.py already proves the FORMULAS and their economic invariants. What it does not prove -- and what the 20260920 production-tree rollback destroyed -- is that the extension layer is ANCHORED: that the eight specs are actually mounted on the registry the product builds, that model_extensions.py exists as real version-controlled content, and that the driver_bounds mechanism survives. A formula suite cannot detect a lost mount, because the formulas still pass in isolation.
deliverable.independent_oracle: The eight model names are the card pack's frozen identity list, not values read back from the registry under test; the bounds assertions are derived from the card text. No expected value is produced by calling the code under test.

lesson: A task marked complete is not the same as a deliverable that LANDED. A working-tree file has no history: `git log -- <path>` empty + an on-disk file = an unlanded artefact. When closing a card, verify the deliverable is COMMITTED, not merely present.
